subject: Agriculture
title: Carbon Credits for Farmers
description: One-minute skill: Carbon Credits for Farmers.

hook.text: Companies pay farmers to store carbon in their soil. It sounds like free money—but the details are complicated.

buildup.text: Carbon markets let corporations offset emissions by funding agricultural practices that sequester CO₂ in soil.

discovery.text: Cover crops, no-till, and composting can sequester 0.5–1 ton of CO₂ per hectare per year.

twist.text: Measuring soil carbon accurately is expensive and uncertain. How do you verify what's underground across millions of acres?

climax.text: Some carbon credits may be overestimated or impermanent—if a farmer plows again, the stored carbon is released.

punchline.text: Paying farmers for carbon is a great idea—if we can measure it honestly.

quiz.question: What's the main challenge with agricultural carbon credits?
options: Measuring soil carbon accurately and ensuring permanence is difficult
